title: Revolutionizing Vaccine Distribution and Surveillance in Cameroon Through Artificial Intelligence
content: Cameroon's Expanded Programme on Immunization continues to face persistent structural obstacles, including unreliable cold chain infrastructure, fragmented data systems, and constrained funding, all of which limit the country's ability to deliver vaccines equitably and to detect disease outbreaks promptly. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including machine learning, computer vision, geospatial analytics, and natural language processing, are increasingly being deployed across Sub-Saharan Africa to strengthen supply chain forecasting, automate cold chain monitoring, accelerate outbreak detection, and improve the quality of routine health information systems such as DHIS2. This review synthesizes the current state of vaccine distribution and surveillance in Cameroon, examines how AI technologies are being applied in comparable African settings, and considers early Cameroonian initiatives such as the DigiCare AI-for-One-Health collaboration. It further explores the ethical, social, and infrastructural considerations that must accompany AI adoption, including algorithmic bias, data privacy, digital equity, and the risk of deepening rural-urban disparities, before outlining future research directions and policy priorities. We argue that AI holds substantial promise for Cameroon's immunization system. Still, this promise can only be realized through deliberate investment in digital infrastructure, workforce capacity, locally representative data, and governance frameworks responsive to the Cameroonian context.
